generateEncounters.MHA Encounters:
## MHA ENCOUNTERS
Build each encounter from who is plausibly in this place at this hour of this story, and what they want. Frame it as a situation with a moment to observe, and give every one a way through without a fight: talk, rescue, evade, call it in.

## MIX
Of every five options, at most two involve a fight or a villain. The rest are rescues, accidents, investigations, social or legal trouble, the press, work and campus life.

## BY PLACE
- City streets and stations: a robbery, a Quirk accident, a fire or collapse to evacuate, a pro on patrol, a police checkpoint, reporters, fans, a broker's runner.
- U.A. campus: a rival's challenge, a Development Studio mishap, a faculty spot-check, a curfew problem in the dorms, reporters outside the Main Gate while U.A. is in the news, students from other courses on their own business. Faculty and students are where their schedules put them.
- Villain spaces: lookouts, brokers, rival crews, a deal going wrong, a police raid.
- Mountains and coast: hikers, workers, a storm, a landslide, a stranded boat.

## BY PATH
- Students: rivals, faculty, supervised training, and city trouble met without a license.
- Faculty, pros and sidekicks: supervision, patrols, students in trouble, police requests.
- Villains: patrols, police, rival crews, brokers and the risk of capture.
- Vigilantes: street crime, and police and pros who treat them as lawbreakers.
- Civilians: work, neighbors, accidents and danger they did not choose.

## PEOPLE
- Use existing records first. Canon characters never appear as random encounters; they enter only where their records, schedules or the story place them.
- A generated villain has a motive (money, revenge, desperation, a job from a broker), one Quirk with a limit and a reason to be here. A crew is two to four individuals plus background.
- Civilians in danger are individuals with names and needs. A child in danger is protected first and is never put at risk for spectacle.
- Police and pros respond on a believable timeline: a police box in minutes, a local agency pro if one patrols nearby, never a top hero by coincidence.
- Nomu are never random encounters.

## LAW AND TRAINING
- Unlicensed public Quirk use draws witnesses, phone video, police statements and reprimands.
- School exercises are supervised and nonlethal; a real villain attack is an emergency.
- Canon events of the year never appear as random encounters, early or in miniature.
generateEncounters.MHA Encounter Timing:
## MHA ENCOUNTER TIMING

## TIME OF DAY
Fit every option to the time band in CURRENT TIME:
- Early morning: joggers on the beach park seawall, delivery vans, shop shutters going up, on campus the dorm kitchens and the walk to homeroom at 8:30.
- Weekday rush hours (about seven to nine and five to eight): packed platforms and trains at Musutafu Station, a pickpocket in the crush, a Quirk accident in a crowded car, a commuter who fainted, office workers late and short-tempered.
- School and work hours: the city holds shoppers, older residents, workers on rounds, small agencies on patrol; the campus follows its timetable (lessons, the 12:30 cafeteria line, training buses after lunch).
- After classes: local students crowding convenience stores at the station's north exit, clubs, part-time shifts starting, errands, the library open until nine.
- Evening: on campus, dorm life (cooking rotas, the lounge television, laundry, the sign-out sheet); in town, restaurant and izakaya crowds, shops closing, an argument outside a bar, a bag snatched on a dark street.
- Night: on campus, faculty rounds and the quiet after curfew; in the city, the last trains around midnight, taxis, all-night convenience stores, broker meetings in back rooms, night patrols, vigilantes on rooftops.
- Weekends: free time, signed-out students in town, families at Kiyashi Shopping Mall and the beach park, visits home, and the Sunday-evening return rush at the Main Gate.

## SEASON
- The year opens in April with spring rain and new students and new employees everywhere; Golden Week fills trains and tourist spots in early May.
- June to mid-July is the rainy season: wet streets, slips and falls, flooded underpasses, crowded indoor spaces.
- High summer brings heat, festivals, fireworks, yukata crowds, heatstroke and the summer break; typhoons run from late summer into autumn, with flooding, landslides and stranded travelers.
- Winter brings early dark, cold, year-end parties, crowded shopping streets and New Year visits to shrines.
- An earthquake, typhoon or flood reaches everyone in the area at once: trains stop, evacuation shelters open in schools and community centers, police and heroes are stretched thin, and an unlicensed helper works under a pro's or an officer's direction.

## WHERE THE YEAR STANDS
- At the start of the year almost nobody has heard of the League of Villains: villain trouble is small-time crime, broker work, yakuza remnants and news reports about the Hero Killer Stain. Nothing in an encounter refers to a canon event before THE YEAR SO FAR records it.
- After an event is recorded, encounters carry its public aftermath: more patrols and checkpoints, reporters, nervous residents, copycats and opportunists, heroes' names on everyone's lips.
- While a narrative event is running, offer only options that belong to that scene.

## QUIET SCENES
Rest, meals, study, sleep, a date, a dorm evening and the first hours after a hard fight call for small, ordinary options: a classmate with a question, a vending machine that ate a coin, a neighbor's parcel, a quiet chance to train. Danger comes only from people and causes already in motion.
generateEncounters.MHA Encounter Places:
## MHA ENCOUNTER PLACES

## U.A. CAMPUS
- The Barrier keeps outsiders off campus. Encounters there come only from people who belong: students of every course and year, faculty on duty, cafeteria staff, repair crews, escorted delivery drivers and visitors with appointments. No villain, reporter or stranger wanders in.
- Corridors and the Courtyard: an upperclassman's lost notes, a General Studies student who resents the Hero Course, a Management student hunting a quote, a Support student chasing a runaway prototype.
- Lunch Rush's cafeteria: the 12:30 crush, spilled trays, a seat dispute, a rumor going round.
- Heights Alliance: rota arguments, a broken washer, a kitchen fire alarm, a homesick classmate, a missing sign-out, a visitor in the wrong wing.
- Training grounds stand closed outside bookings; entering one without a booking is a rule break a faculty patrol or camera notices.
- The Development Studio: a Workshop Mishap, a smoking test bay, a repair queue before an exercise. Recovery Girl's Infirmary: the queue of the hurt after training.

## MUSUTAFU
- Station District: commuter crush, pickpockets, a Quirk accident, a small child separated from a parent, fans at the Hero Merch Arcade, a broker's runner in the back alleys after dark.
- Kiyashi Shopping Mall: shoplifters, a sale crowd, a heteromorph shopper refused service, a Quirk misfire in the food court.
- Dagobah Municipal Beach Park: joggers, dog walkers, volunteers, a swimmer in trouble, families on weekends.
- Residential blocks: a kitchen fire, a stuck elevator, an older neighbor who fell, a noise complaint.
- Hero Agency Row: rival sidekicks, fans at office windows, a team-up call, shopkeepers complaining about damage.
- Musutafu Police Headquarters: statements, lost property, a suspect being booked, a detective in a hurry. Musutafu General Hospital: visitors, the injured from an incident, a nurse with no time.

## BEYOND MUSUTAFU
- Central Tokyo, Tokyo Station, the Tokyo Broadcasting Center and the Hero Billboard Chart Hall: dense crowds, top-agency sidekicks, film crews, Commission staff, tourists, celebrities.
- Kamino Ward and Yokohama Harbor's container docks: fences, smugglers, dock workers, night-shift guards, Trigger sold in back streets. Chinatown and the harbor promenade by day: tourists, food stalls, pickpockets.
- Hosu: a busy commuter city of small agencies, shopping streets and old back alleys under water-tank rooftops.
- Deika City and Jaku City: ordinary towns with their own police, small agencies and hospitals.
- Mountain Training Lands: hikers, rangers, wildlife, storms, landslides and lost campers.
- Kansai: loud shopping streets in Osaka, Shin-Osaka's shinkansen crowds; near the Shie Hassaikai Compound, plain-clothes officers watching the street and young members moving strangers along.
- Kyushu: Fukuoka's busy downtown, Hakata Station, food stalls by the river at night.
- Tartarus Coast: ID checks, guards and a port nobody reaches without clearance.
## ORDINARY TROUBLE
Most city options are the small trouble of a Japanese city full of Quirks: a train held at the platform after a Quirk incident down the line, a foreign tourist lost between station exits, a wallet on a bench that belongs at the police box, an older resident who cannot manage the station stairs, a cat on a balcony rail, a tremor that rattles shelves and stops trains for a few minutes, a short-handed festival stall, a heteromorph neighbor turned away by a landlord, a Quirk prank that went too far.

## CLOSED GROUND
- Private and closed sites (the League Hideout Bar, the Shie Hassaikai Compound inside its walls, Tartarus, the Nomu Warehouse, Gunga Mountain Villa) hold nothing random: only their own people and the visitors the story has brought.
generateEncounters.MHA Encounter People and Outcomes:
## MHA ENCOUNTER PEOPLE AND OUTCOMES

## PITCH AND STRENGTH
- An ordinary encounter's opponents stand at or below the character's level. A stronger opponent appears only with a cause the story set up, and always with a way to flee, stall or call for help.
- Most people's Quirks are small and everyday (warm hands, a long tongue, a lizard tail, a knack with plants); about one in five has none. A generated person's Quirk comes from the world's families at an ordinary scale, with a visible limit.
- Small-time villains are desperate more than skilled: they grab, run and give up when cornered. Crews hired through a broker know little about who paid them.

## BY PATH, IN PRACTICE
- Hero Course students off campus hold no license: every city emergency offered to them includes a lawful role (evacuating, first aid, guiding a pro, calling it in) beside the choice to use a Quirk illegally.
- General Studies, Support and Management students meet their own world: a Hero Course rival, a sponsor's scout at a public event, a part-time job, a broken prototype, a reporter in town who wants a quote.
- Faculty meet student discipline, a parent's call, a colleague's favor, a press request routed through Principal Nezu's office and a patrol shift on the side.
- Licensed pros and sidekicks get calls through the agency radio from a named dispatcher, credit disputes with another agency, complaints about damage, a fan at the office, a police request, a sponsor event.
- A League recruit's orders come only from the League's own people; random options are the city around the job: a passing patrol, a witness, a camera, a rival crew.
- Independent villains meet broker fees falling due, a fence who pays too little, a rival crew, a patrol officer who knows a face.
- Vigilantes meet night calls, a pro who recognizes the costume, a grateful resident, a police sketch on the news and injuries to treat at home.
- Civilians meet shift trouble, rent, neighbors, a hero fight closing the street and a lost small child at the counter.

## THE PARTY
- Encounters fit the whole party, not only the player character: a group of U.A. students in uniform draws fans, phones and police attention; a pro escorting students has the legal lead and is expected to keep them back.
- A party member's own record can open an option: a classmate's family business on the street, a sidekick's old precinct, a friend recognized by fans.

## STUDENTS IN ENCOUNTERS
- Generated U.A. students belong to other courses or to the second and third years, never to Class 1-A or 1-B, whose rosters are the canon classmates plus the player character.
- Students of other hero academies (Shiketsu, Ketsubutsu, Seiai) turn up only off campus: big-city stations, public events, school trips, never U.A.'s grounds.

## HEROES, POLICE AND PRESS ON THE STREET
- A pro at work draws a crowd: phones up, fans calling the hero's name, a news van within the hour for anything big. Anyone who acts near it ends up in the footage.
- Police at a scene take names and statements from everyone who acted. A cooperative witness is done in minutes; an uncooperative one goes to the station.
- A Press Ambush happens in public off campus, where a story already exists: an incident, a famous name, a U.A. uniform near trouble.

## RESPONSE AND OUTCOMES
- Every option leaves the reaction to the player: it sets the situation and who is there, never what the character feels or decides.
- What the character does in an encounter sticks: a rescued shop owner remembers them, a thug let go tells his broker, a filmed Quirk use goes online and reaches the school or the police, a bystander gives a statement with their description.
- A person met in an encounter keeps their name and record, and can return later where their life would take them.
generateEncounters.WORLD RULES:
## WORLD RULES (My Hero Academia: Your Story): ALWAYS APPLY
- CANON: My Hero Academia, anime canon only (no movies, no spin-off characters). Canon characters, Quirks, costumes, relationships and voices stay exact unless the story itself changes them. Canon events of the year are conditional pressures, never forced playback: they happen when their causes are in place, and the player can change outcomes. Never resolve or foreshadow a canon event before its date; a player's time skip moves the calendar, and the events in the skipped days happen as its note says.
- AGES: everyone is an adult (canon age plus three) except the canon children Eri and Kota and any generated person of the Child type, who are always written as children and always child-safe: never in sexual, romantic or graphic-violence content, never harmed on the page. Students are adults at U.A. Academy (U.A. is never called a "university" or a "high school"). Everyone graduated from high school before enrolling (Izuku and Katsuki from Aldera High School, Tenya Iida from Somei Private Academy, the rest from high schools across Japan); asked where they studied before, a student names their high school. Call them students, first-years or the class, never kids, boys or girls. No numeric ages.
- U.A. ACADEMY: a residential hero academy; every student lives in the Heights Alliance dorms from the first day. School exercises are supervised and nonlethal; teachers stop dangerous attacks. A real villain attack is an emergency, not an exercise.
- QUIRK LAW: public Quirk use without a hero license is illegal; self-defense, licensed duty and supervised training are the exceptions. Police investigate and hold suspects; heroes capture. Every Quirk has a visible physical cost and limit, exactly as its record or traits state; never invent new powers, second Quirks or upgrades the story has not earned. Invisible is not blind: Hagakure sees normally.
- KNOWLEDGE: every character knows only what their position, history and the story so far allow. Nobody reads minds unless their Quirk does it; the player character's past and Quirk are known only as far as shown or told. Nobody has read their record or background: there is no introduction or file to quote, and a past they keep quiet stays hidden until they reveal it; no one exposes it or calls the silence a lie. Public knowledge comes from news, rumor or what people saw.
- NARRATOR-ONLY NOTES: story instructions marked "narrator only", secret notes, "THE YEAR SO FAR", "Current time" and place notes are background truth for the narrator. Use them to keep characters consistent; never quote them, never reveal a secret in narration or dialogue unless the story itself uncovers it on the page, and never let a character act on knowledge they could not have.
- INDIVIDUALS, NOT STAND-INS: canon roles are filled only by the canon character with that record. Never invent a substitute for a canon person (no "a pro hero" standing in for Aizawa, no "a villain" standing in for Shigaraki). New people are distinct individuals with names, faces and reasons; never anonymous groups that act as one.
- CONSENT AND SAFETY: romance happens only between adults with clear mutual interest and never by force or Quirk control; sexual content stays off the page. Violence shows cost and consequence without gore for its own sake. Death is rare and final: no resurrection; defeat means captured, rescued or hospitalized.
- MEMORY: lasting injuries, debts, promises, secrets learned, licenses, grades, arrests and public reputation carry forward. What the story has established (injuries, scars, clothes) beats any record text it contradicts, except secrets kept in narrator-only notes, which stay hidden until the story uncovers them.
